parts.problem_md:
A rock has a mass of 20 kg. The rock is at rest at a height of 5.0 m above the ground.

It then falls to the ground.

What is the speed of the rock just before it hits the ground?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- Using $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2 a s$ with $u = 0$:

$v^{2} = 2 \times 9 . 8 \times 5 . 0$

$v^{2} = 98$

$v = \sqrt{98} \approx 9 . 9 \text{m} / \text{s}$

parts.problem_md:
Fig. 7.1 shows a speed–time graph for a student walking to school.

![Speed–time graph: speed rises from 0 to 1.5 m/s by 35 s, stays constant until 100 s, then decreases back to 0 m/s at 120 s.](assets/001-speed-time-graph-speed-rises-from-0-to-1-5-m-s-b.png)

**Fig. 7.1**

(i) Determine the time taken by the student to reach maximum speed.

[1]

(ii) On Fig. 7.1, write an X at a point on the graph when the student is decelerating.

[1]

(iii) Determine the distance the student walks at constant speed.

[3]
parts.solution_md:
(i)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - 40 s **[1 mark]**

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - X marked on the graph line at any point between 100 s and 120 s **[1 mark]**

(iii)

To calculate the distance walked at constant speed:

- List the known quantities:

- Speed, v = 1.5 m/s (read from the graph between 40 s and 100 s)
- Time, t = 100 - 40 = 60 s

- Write down the equation:

$\text{distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time}$

- Substitute the known values:

$\text{distance} = 1 . 5 \times 60$ **[1 mark]**

- Calculate the answer:

distance = **90 m** **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for correctly identifying the graph data between 40 s and 100 s, using a speed of 1.5 m/s
> 
> 1 mark for correct use of distance = speed × time (or equivalent use of the area under the graph)
> 
> 1 mark for a correct final answer of 90 m
> 
> - Marks must be awarded in this order

> **[exam-tip]**
> On a speed–time graph, deceleration is shown by a downward-sloping section — mark your point anywhere along that section, not just at the start or end. For distance at constant speed, remember you can either multiply speed by time or find the area under the flat section of the graph — both give the same answer.

parts.problem_md:
(i) A spacecraft has a mass of 3.1 × 10<sup>3</sup> kg.

Calculate the weight of the spacecraft on the surface of the Earth.

Include the unit in your answer.

[3]

(ii) The spacecraft is launched into space. The spacecraft accelerates as it moves upwards through the Earth’s atmosphere.

State what is meant by accelerates.

[1]

(iii) The spacecraft travels from the Earth to the Moon in 3.2 days.

Calculate the number of hours in 3.2 days.

[1]

(iv) The distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384 000 km.

Use your answer to (a)(iii) to calculate the average speed of the spacecraft in km/h.

[2]

(v) The spacecraft is controlled by radio waves sent from the Earth.

State whether the radio waves travel to the spacecraft faster, slower or at the same speed as visible light.

Give a reason for your answer.

speed: ..........................................................................................................

reason: .........................................................................................................

[1]
parts.solution_md:
(i)

To calculate the weight of the spacecraft:

- List the known quantities:

- Mass, m = 3.1 × 10<sup>3</sup> kg
- Gravitational field strength, g = 9.8 N kg<sup>-1</sup>

- Write down the equation:

$W = m g$

- Substitute the known values:

$W = 3 . 1 \times 10^{3} \times 9 . 8$ **[1 mark]**

- Calculate the answer:

$W = 30 \times 10^{3}$

W = **30 000 N** **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for correct substitution into $W = m g$ (accept formula in any form)
> 
> 1 mark for a correct intermediate answer of 30 × 10<sup>3</sup> N
> 
> - Accept 30.38 or 30.4
> - Ignore 31
> 
> 1 mark for the correct unit, N or newton(s)

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - increases in speed **[1 mark]**

(iii)

$3 . 2 \times 24 =$ **76.8 h** **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for a correct final answer of 76.8 h
> 
> - Accept 76 h 48 min

(iv)

To calculate the average speed of the spacecraft:

- List the known quantities:

- Distance, s = 384 000 km
- Time, t = 76.8 h

- Write down the equation:

$v = \frac{s}{t}$

- Substitute the known values:

$v = \frac{384000}{76.8}$ **[1 mark]**

- Calculate the answer:

v = **5000 km/h** **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for correct substitution into $v = \frac{s}{t}$ (accept formula in any form)
> 
> 1 mark for a correct final answer of 5000 km/h
> 
> - ecf from (a)(iii)

(v)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - speed: same AND reason: both are electromagnetic waves, which all travel at the same speed **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> When a calculation asks you to "include the unit", the unit itself often carries its own mark — write it clearly next to your final answer. For multi-step calculations like this one, you can use your rounded answer from an earlier part (e.g. part (iii)) in a later substitution — this is allowed under error carried forward (ecf), so one mistake won't cost you marks twice.

parts.problem_md:
The diagrams show four distance–time graphs.

Which graph represents the motion of an object that is at rest?

![Four distance–time graphs A–D: A rising line, B falling line, C horizontal line, D V-shaped line descending then rising, all with distance vertical and time horizontal.](assets/002-four-distance-time-graphs-a-d-a-rising-line-b-fa.png)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- A horizontal line on a distance–time graph shows the distance from the origin stays constant over time, meaning the object is at rest

**A** is incorrect because a rising straight line on a distance–time graph shows constant positive velocity

**B** is incorrect because a falling straight line on a distance–time graph shows constant negative velocity

**D** is incorrect because this graph shows the object moving towards the origin then away from it, indicating changing velocity, not rest
